rationale: Weakness is common enough for a cohort but the exposure must be reconstructed day by day from records, so a case-control design nested in the clinical information system is efficient: all cases and two matched controls each, with exposure counted only on eligible days (c3). Randomised evidence (c1, c2) shows mobilisation matters, but not how partial adherence relates to weakness. The director's day-3 marker (c4) and extra ICU days are kept as secondary descriptive analyses.
alternatives: Full cohort of all ventilated patients (refused: day-by-day exposure extraction for every patient exceeds the research nurse's time)
Diagnostic accuracy study of the day-3 scale as the main study (refused: a different question with a modest answer already)
Cost analysis of weakness (refused as a main aim: attributable stay would be confused with the effect of mobilisation)
guidelines: STROBE for case-control studies with the RECORD extension
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial of adherence strategies would need the association first; the case-control study uses existing records to provide it.

decision.statement: Run a case-control study nested in the ICU clinical information system: cases with ICU-acquired weakness at discharge since March 2025, two controls each matched on ventilation duration, exposure as missed mobilisation on eligible days among the first five, adjusted for severity and deep sedation, with the day-3 marker and extra ICU days as secondary descriptive analyses.
decision.question: How should the unit estimate whether missed early mobilisation is associated with ICU-acquired weakness?

criteria.text: Mobilisation reduces weakness in trials, so missed mobilisation is a plausible exposure.
Confounding by severity can be reduced by counting eligible days and adjusting.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval with a waiver of consent
gates.evidence: Approval REB-2026-0931 dated 2026-09-16, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Release of the clinical information system extract
gates.evidence: ICU director approval ICU-DIR-2026-12 dated 2026-09-18, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Diagnostic accuracy study of the day-3 scale
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; both gates rest on investigator-supplied approvals.

summary: Nested case-control study recommended; decision rests on three ledger claims; gates met.
